MDB-5 used about **908 kWh more** in the week after detection (+4.4%). Note the leak was detected on 2025-09-09 but the leak itself began 2025-09-03 [data: list_detections], so the elevated consumption was already in effect during the "before" window.

**First detection:** 2025-11-03 (the low-power-factor rule fired at 09:08, PF down to 0.84, threshold 0.90) [data: list_detections].

**Average PF 08:00–17:00 that day:** 0.862 (min 0.846, max 0.966 at 08:00) [data: get_meter_series].

The board ran near 0.96 until ~08:35, then dropped to ~0.85 for the rest of the window — consistent with the tripped capacitor bank (incident S8) that took MDB-3 from 0.96 to 0.84 [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-05_power_factor_check.md#SOP-05 Power Factor Check > Reference case: incident S8].

Yes. Peak demand hit **1,324.4 kW at 08:15**, which is 6% over the 1,250 kW contract limit [data: get_demand]. Only two 15-minute intervals exceeded the contract (08:00 at 1,307.1 kW and 08:15 at 1,324.4 kW), right after the Monday morning simultaneous start of the SMT lines and reflow ovens [unverified citation removed].

According to SOP-02 and the reflow oven manual:

**Why OFF, not standby:** A reflow oven in standby draws 36% of its 70 kW rating — 25.2 kW per oven — continuously for as long as it stays on, producing nothing. A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend. The ovens must stay on only 30 minutes after the line stops, then be switched off, and only when no boards are inside.

**S5 cost:** In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend. Weekend energy was about 1,556 kWh against about 346 kWh normal — an excess of about 1,210 kWh from a single oven.

Note: the off-schedule rule only flags this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the real benefit is preventing it before it happens.

Sources: [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby], [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-01_reflow_oven.md#EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual > Energy-saving notes]

answer:
Per SOP-03 Step 2 (shed in playbook order):

**Shed first:** EV charging (pause EV-01, 100% of its load) — it is Action 1 in the playbook order.

**Never shed:** the server room, running molders mid-cycle, or reflow ovens with boards inside.

The full shed order is: (1) pause EV charging, (2) delay next burn-in loading (BI-01/BI-02), (3) raise chilled-water setpoint +1°C, (4) lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar. Restore in reverse order once demand is stable below 1,125 kW.

[source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]
